items.statement: Where residual solvent levels above the guideline limits are applied (for example short-term use of 30 days or less, or topical application), justify these higher levels case by case.
items.quote: Higher levels of residual solvents may be acceptable in certain cases such as short term (30 days or less) or topical application. Justification for these levels should be made on a case by case basis.

items.statement: Where Class 1 solvents are likely to be present, identify and quantify them.
items.quote: If Class 1 solvents are likely to be present, they should be identified and quantified.
items.condition: Class 1 solvents likely to be present

items.statement: Where Class 2 solvents exceed their Option 1 limits, or Class 3 solvents exceed 0.5%, identify and quantify them.
items.quote: If solvents of Class 2 or Class 3 are present at greater than their Option 1 limits or 0.5%, respectively, they should be identified and quantified.
items.condition: Class 2 above Option 1 limit or Class 3 above 0.5%

items.statement: Do not use Class 1 solvents in manufacturing drug substances, excipients or drug products.
items.quote: Solvents in Class 1 should not be employed in the manufacture of drug substances, excipients, and drug products because of their unacceptable toxicity or their deleterious environmental effect.

items.statement: If use of a Class 1 solvent cannot be avoided to make a drug product with a significant therapeutic advance, restrict Benzene to 2 ppm, unless otherwise justified.

items.condition: Class 1 use unavoidable for significant therapeutic advance; unless otherwise justified
